definition.text: The polluter pays principle says that whoever causes pollution should pay for the damage it does to the environment.

facts.text: It has also been used to make polluters bear the cost of preventing pollution.
Economics supports it: assigning all costs of a decision, including pollution harm, to the decision-maker removes externalities and is a condition for Pareto efficiency.
It underpins policies such as ecotaxes, and cap-and-trade schemes apply it by making polluters buy allowances to cover their emissions.
It is principle 16 of the 1992 Rio Declaration, though not binding in all areas of international environmental law.
It is used in all the major US pollution laws, including the Clean Air Act, the Clean Water Act and Superfund.
Historian Jean-Baptiste Fressoz notes that paying compensation for pollution was already the rule favored by 19th-century industrialists.
It has been doubted where nobody knew a pollutant was dangerous when it was emitted, as with early industrial carbon dioxide.

definition.text: Extended producer responsibility makes producers bear the environmental costs of their products over the whole product life, mainly in waste management.

facts.text: It shifts the duty of handling waste from governments and taxpayers to the firms that make the products.
By building disposal costs into the product price, it should lead producers to design products with less waste and more reuse and recycling.
Thomas Lindhqvist probably first described the concept for the Swedish government in 1990.

title: Carbon fee and dividend

definition.text: Carbon fee and dividend taxes fossil fuels for their carbon and pays the money back to everyone in equal per-person payments.

facts.text: The fee is charged where fuels enter the economy, such as the well, mine or port, and rises over time to give a predictable price signal.
A border adjustment charges imports from countries without an equivalent carbon fee.
Returning all net fees makes the scheme revenue-neutral, which appeals to those who do not want government to grow.
Paying out the revenue as a universal climate income largely offsets the higher prices a carbon tax causes.
As of July 2022 eight jurisdictions used a form of it, including Switzerland, Austria and several Canadian provinces.
Switzerland returns about two-thirds of its carbon tax revenue through health insurance bills, but a 2019 survey found only 11.8% of residents knew most funds were redistributed.
A 2021 study of Canada and Switzerland found that returning the money did little to make carbon taxes more popular.

related: Energy Innovation and Carbon Dividend Act

definition.text: Environmental pricing reform, or ecological fiscal reform, adjusts market prices through taxes or subsidies so they reflect environmental costs and benefits.

facts.text: It responds to externalities: when prices leave out environmental costs, self-interested choices can harm the environment and distort the economy.
Each market-based instrument, such as ecotaxes, tradeable pollution permits or paying for ecological services, is one instance of it.
It can cover the whole economy or focus on one sector or one problem such as climate change.
Environmental tax reform began in the Nordic countries in the early 1990s and spread to the Netherlands, Germany and the United Kingdom.
IMF economists found that a tax 50% above or below marginal damage still captures about three quarters of the welfare gain, so broad coverage matters more than precision.
The World Bank reported carbon pricing revenue rose from under $30 billion in 2016 to more than $107 billion in 2025.

definition.text: Price-based instruments such as taxes fix the price of pollution and let the amount vary, while quantity-based instruments such as cap-and-trade fix the amount and let the price vary.

facts.text: In theory the two give the same result when pollution and costs match expectations, but they diverge when they do not.
Emissions trading sets a limit and lets permits be traded among emitters, while a carbon tax sets a price.
A 2018 survey found 58% of leading economists agreed carbon taxes are better than cap-and-trade, and none disagreed.

definition.text: Revenue recycling means using the money raised by an environmental tax to cut other taxes or return it to people, rather than adding it to general spending.

facts.text: How the revenue is used greatly affects the economic cost of an environmental tax reform.
If revenue is not used to cut distorting taxes or is badly spent, the overall benefits fall quickly.
Recycling revenue makes a carbon tax revenue-neutral, for example by lowering income tax or paying citizens a dividend.
Using a tax's revenue to reduce other distorting taxes is what opens the possibility of a double dividend.
IMF authors warn that dedicated funds can lead governments to set rates by the fund's needs instead of by actual damage.
The UK Climate Change Levy dropped revenue recycling in 2010, sending the money to the Exchequer.

title: Fossil fuel subsidy reform
article: Environmental pricing reform#Fossil Fuel subsidy reform

definition.text: Fossil fuel subsidy reform removes subsidies that keep fossil fuel prices below their supply cost or below their full environmental cost.

facts.text: The IMF separates explicit subsidies, where consumer prices are below supply cost, from implicit ones, where prices omit environmental damage.
Explicit subsidies reached 1.3% of global GDP in 2022 and fell to 0.6% in 2024, the IMF estimated.
Removing fossil fuel subsidies counts as an implicit carbon price.

definition.text: A deposit-refund system adds a surcharge when a product is bought and pays it back when the product or its packaging is returned.

facts.text: It works like a Pigouvian tax that is refunded once the product is returned, rewarding proper disposal.
Beverage containers are the usual case, but it is also used for batteries, tyres, motor oil, electronics and shipping pallets.
It discourages illegal dumping, eases monitoring and is hard to evade.
It can end up favoring single-use packaging over refillable systems, as in Germany.
It is said to rest on the principles of extended producer responsibility.
